onColors settles shares on the colour Effected writes below truecolor (rich-effects-x7y0)

Below truecolor, `shares` checked contrast against `fromRgba(...).downgrade(depth)`
while `Effected` wrote `ColorSpec.matchOn` for the cell's slot, keeping the
written spec when the depth could not show the move. The two disagreed at 256
and 16 colours, so a word could fall below its resting contrast or AA.

The rule now lives once, as `ColorSpec.matchMove`, and both sides call it.
`Pair` gains `reverse`, so each side is matched in the slot it is written in.

The effect catalogue is one named table with one call shape (rich-effects-cbgp.ydw) (#396)

* The effect catalogue is one named table with one call shape (rich-effects-cbgp.ydw)

EFFECT_CATALOGUE makes every catalogue effect by its EFFECT_CURVES name:
`loops` as Effects, `transitions` as Transitions, each called as
(element: EffectTarget, curve?) with the signed-off curve, light and width
built in. Keyed by LoopName/TransitionName, derived from EFFECT_CURVES, so a
curve signed off without an entry does not compile.

To make that one call shape true, fadeIn and dissolveOut take (curve, z):
every effect runs on its own clock from t = 0, and a veil blends toward
Drawn.theme's background, the terminal Effected already names, instead of a
second ground handed in. SHIMMER_WIDTH leaves the barrel; the catalogue
carries it.

The effects-feel demo and its legibility test draw through the catalogue,
and the playground binds each card to its factory function rather than a
name in a string.

* Review fixes for the effect catalogue (rich-effects-cbgp.ydw)

- docs: a fade-in is not at rest at t = 0; say only that every effect runs on
  its own clock from there. A shimmer made by hand takes its own reach.
- LoopName is spelled out beside TransitionName, and EFFECT_CURVES is held to
  both, so a new curve does not compile until it is placed in a section,
  instead of defaulting to a loop.
- The playground names each card's function by a shorthand key, not its
  runtime .name, which a bundler renames on a collision.
- effects-feel builds its transitions once per scene, as it does its loops.
Whole-keys settle reads a chunk's rest in full when a sink throws mid-drain (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Whole-keys settle: ESC [ / ESC O is the Alt chord; settling survives a throwing sink (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Review fixes: whole-keys feed no longer runs the split hold logic; header
names InputChunks; docs Input field typed; integration test that a
NodeTerminalHost in the docs worker reads whole-keys. Split-host residue
filed as rich-host-input-gnl7.

A whole-keys host settles each input chunk; no lone ESC is held for a timer (rich-host-input-ab9n)

TerminalHost declares inputChunks: xterm.js (BrowserTerminalHost, and the
docs worker's simulated stdin through NodeTerminalHost) never splits a key
across chunks, so an ESC left at a chunk's end is Escape and what followed
it is re-read. A tty stays "split" and keeps the setTimeout(0) hold.
